item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
[Image: A spinner, which is divided and labeled with purple, orange, green, blue, and red. The purple section takes up half of the spinner. The orange section takes up one fourth of the spinner. The green, blue, and red sections each take up one twelfth of the spinner.]

The spinner is for Steve's new game. Out of 600 spins, approximately how many times should he expect the arrow to land on the red sector?
item.figure_description: A circular spinner with a central pivot dot and an arrow pointing toward the upper right. The circle is divided into five sectors by radius lines. A vertical diameter splits the circle: the entire right half is a single semicircle labeled 'Purple'. The top-left quadrant is labeled 'Orange'. The bottom-left quadrant is divided into three equal slices, labeled from top to bottom as 'Green', 'Blue', and 'Red'.
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Spinner]

Roland’s spinner has three sectors of different colors, orange, purple, and green. Roland spins the pointer 1000 times. The chart below shows how many times the pointer stops on each section.

| Color | Times Stopped |
| :--- | :---: |
| Orange | 510 |
| Purple | 243 |
| Green | 247 |

Draw lines on the spinner above to make the three sectors the approximate size you would expect them to be. Label them orange, purple, and green.

descriptors: Orange sector approximately half the circle, green and purple each approximately one-quarter, all correctly labeled
Only one labeled sector the correct size
Three sectors drawn but none the correct size
Three sectors of correct size drawn but no labels
Other incorrect (including crossed out/erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)

reference_items.figure_description: A circular spinner with a central circular hub and an arrow pointer angled upward and to the right. Around the circumference of the circle is an outer rim with 8 equally spaced tick marks, dividing the circle into 8 equal arcs of 45° each (at 12 o'clock, 1:30, 3 o'clock, 4:30, 6 o'clock, 7:30, 9 o'clock, and 10:30). The interior of the circle is blank.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
The figure below shows a spinner with 24 sectors. When someone spins the arrow, it is equally likely to stop on any sector.

[Image: Spinner with 24 sectors]

1/8 of the sectors are blue, 1/24 are purple, 1/2 are orange, and 1/3 are red. If a person spins the arrow, on which color sector is the spinner LEAST likely to stop?
reference_items.figure_description: A circular spinner divided equally into 24 sectors by radial line segments from a central pivot point. An arrow is mounted at the center, pointing toward the sector at approximately the 1 o'clock position. The sectors are plain white and unlabeled.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Rectangle divided into 12 squares with some squares shaded]

Which circle has approximately the same fraction of its area shaded as the rectangle above?
reference_items.figure_description:
At the top, a rectangle is divided into a grid of 3 rows and 4 columns, forming 12 equal-sized squares. The bottom row has all 4 squares shaded gray. The middle row has the leftmost square shaded gray and the other 3 squares unshaded (white). The top row has all 4 squares unshaded. In total, 5 of the 12 squares are shaded.

Each option shows a circle with a center point and radial lines dividing it into sectors, with one sector shaded gray:
- Option A: The circle is divided by a vertical radius pointing up (12 o'clock) and another radius pointing down and slightly left (about 6:30). The larger sector on the right side is shaded gray (covering slightly more than half of the circle).
- Option B: The circle is divided by a vertical diameter passing through the center from 12 o'clock to 6 o'clock. The right half of the circle is shaded gray (exactly 1/2 of the circle).
- Option C: The circle is divided by a vertical radius pointing up (12 o'clock) and a horizontal radius pointing left (9 o'clock). The sector extending clockwise from 12 o'clock to 9 o'clock is shaded gray (3/4 of the circle).
- Option D: The circle is divided by a vertical radius pointing up (12 o'clock) and another radius pointing down and to the right (about 4:30 to 5 o'clock). The sector between them on the right side is shaded gray (covering somewhat less than half of the circle, approximately 5/12 of the area).
- Option E: The circle is divided by a vertical radius pointing up (12 o'clock) and another radius pointing up and slightly left (about 11 o'clock). The major sector extending clockwise from 12 o'clock to 11 o'clock is shaded gray (covering almost the entire circle, about 11/12 of the area).
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Color of Caps

[Image: A pie chart indicating 30% white caps, 25% green caps, 15% black caps, 10% blue caps, and 20% red caps.]

The pie chart shows the percentage of caps for sale at a sporting goods store. If there are 200 caps, what is the total number of caps that are either white or green?
reference_items.figure_description: A pie chart titled "Color of Caps" divided into five sectors: White (labeled "White 30%") occupying the top-left sector; Green (labeled "Green 25%") occupying the top-right quadrant; Red (labeled "Red 20%") occupying the bottom-right sector; Blue (labeled "Blue 10%") occupying a narrow sector at the bottom; and Black (labeled "Black 15%") occupying the sector between Blue and White on the lower left.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
What fraction of the circle is shaded?

[Image: A circle divided into two sectors, one shaded and one unshaded]
reference_items.figure_description: A circle with a center dot. Two radii divide the circle into two sectors. One radius extends straight up from the center to the 12 o'clock position. The other radius extends to the left, slightly below the horizontal 9 o'clock position. The larger sector, which runs clockwise from the top radius around through the right side and bottom to the lower-left radius, is shaded solid gray. The smaller remaining sector in the upper-left area is white (unshaded).
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
On the map, 1 cm represents 10 km on the land.

[Image: Map showing towns and roads]

On the land, about how far apart are the towns Melville and Folley?
reference_items.figure_description: A rectangular map showing three towns marked with dots: Melville near the top center, Mockem on the middle left, and Folley to the lower right. A thick curved black line representing "Red River" runs diagonally across the map from the lower-left to the upper-right. Thin lines represent roads: one goes vertically down through Melville and Mockem, and another connects Melville curving down and to the right, crossing the Red River and passing through Folley. In the bottom right corner of the map, an inset box contains a scale line segment marked with vertical end-ticks labeled "1 cm = 10 km". On the map, the straight-line distance between Melville and Folley is approximately 5 times the length of the 1 cm scale bar.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem: Over recent weeks, a shop’s average sales of bottles of soda have been 50% in the regular size, 40% in the small size, and 10% in the large size. Next week, the shopkeeper will order 1,200 bottles of soda. How many of these bottles should he order in the regular size?
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem: A bowl contains 36 colored beads all of the same size: some blue, some green, some red, and the rest yellow. A bead is drawn from the bowl without looking. The probability that it is blue is 4/9. How many blue beads are in the bowl?
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
If a fair coin is tossed, the probability that it will land heads up is 1/2. In four successive tosses, a fair coin lands heads up each time.
What is likely to happen when the coin is tossed a fifth time?

options.label: A
options.text: It is more likely to land tails up than heads up.

options.label: B
options.text: It is more likely to land heads up than tails up.

options.label: C
options.text: It is equally likely to land heads up or tails up.

options.label: D
options.text: More information is needed to answer the question.

reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: A rectangle]

A. On the grid below, draw a rectangle whose length is three-fourths the length of the rectangle above, and whose width is two and one-half times the width of the rectangle above. Label the length and width of the new rectangle in centimeters on the figure. Each square on the grid is 1 cm by 1 cm.

[Image: A grid of squares]

descriptors: 6 cm and 5 cm. Rectangle is correctly drawn and labeled (on the figure).
Rectangle is correctly labeled, 6 cm and 5 cm, but drawing is incorrect.
Correct drawing is shown, but the length and/or width is not labeled or is incorrectly labeled.
One side is 6 cm and other side is incorrect, explicitly written or implicit from the drawing.
One side is 5 cm and other side is incorrect, explicitly written or implicit from the drawing.
Other incorrect (including crossed out/erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task). Also includes responses in which the drawing is missing.

reference_items.scoring_notes: Note: There is no distinction made between responses with or without units.
reference_items.figure_description: At the top of the page is a rectangle drawn horizontally. Inside near the bottom edge is the word "Length", and below the bottom edge is labeled "8 cm". Along the inside right edge, printed vertically, is "Width" and "2 cm". Below Part A is a dashed-line grid measuring 10 squares wide by 15 squares high.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration.
